hypothesis.claim: A frozen coordinate factor-base family may retain at least 0.9x coordinate-null D5_new support while reducing both exact D2 and D3 supports to at most 0.8x.
hypothesis.mechanism: Coordinate additive geometry creates reusable intermediate point sums without relying on inverse-cancellation padding or proportionally collapsing genuinely new five-term support.
predictions: At least one candidate has D5_nonidentity and D5_new ratios at least 0.9 against both random-x and source-PRF-x medians.
The same candidate has separate D2 and D3 support ratios at most 0.8.
The point-only signal survives public scan-order diagnostics and lies in the lower 5 percent tail of each coordinate null under a preregistered scalar effect statistic.
A promoted signal replicates on at least 75 percent of expanded cells across four sizes and at least two seeds.
hypothesis.falsification: Narrow a family if compression loses D5_new coverage, is reproduced by either coordinate null, depends on scan order, or requires scalar-census or D4/D5 state.
hypothesis.test_boundary: Generated ordinary prime-order toy curves restricted to p mod 4 = 3, frozen factor-base families, exact five-term support, and point-only Stage-A MITM lookup.
